title: Probiotic modulation of the neonatal gut-lung axis in the regulation of early respiratory function.
abstract: The gut -lung axis represents bidirectional communication between the gastrointestinal and respiratory systems that contributes to immune regulation and inflammatory homeostasis. This study evaluated the effects of probiotic-conditioned media (PCM) and live probiotics on epithelial barrier function, inflammatory responses, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial function using Caco-2 intestinal epithelial and A549 pulmonary epithelial cell models under inflammatory conditions.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

title: Disrupting Salmonella colonization and resistance: probiotic cell-free supernatants inhibit biofilm formation and invasion in meat and human isolates.
abstract: Salmonella enterica remains a paramount global public health threat due to the rapid emergence of multi-drug and pan-drug resistant (PDR) strains transmitted through the food supply chain. This study adopted a One Health cross-sectional framework to investigate the occurrence and biocontrol of PDR Salmonella enterica serovars (S. Enteritidis, S. Kentucky, and S. Anatum) isolated from clinical gastroenteritis cases and retail meat products in Egypt.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

title: Prophylactic administration of probiotic strains Weizmannia coagulans and Saccharomyces boulardii attenuates early dysplastic changes in an AOM/DSS-induced mouse model.
abstract: Colorectal dysplasia represents an early stage of colorectal carcinogenesis and is closely associated with chronic inflammation and altered microRNA (miRNA) expression. Probiotic strains such as Weizmannia coagulans (formerly Bacillus coagulans) and Saccharomyces boulardii possess anti-inflammatory properties and may influence host miRNA expression, suggesting their potential as prophylactic agents against inflammation-associated colorectal dysplasia.

title: Probiotics as a Strategy for Mitigating Viral Infections in Poultry: Immunomodulatory Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential.
abstract: Poultry viral infections remain a persistent challenge for the poultry industry, causing significant economic losses and posing potential threats to human health. The escalating frequency of outbreaks involving pathogens, such as infectious bronchitis virus (IBV), Newcastle disease virus (NDV) and avian influenza virus (AIV), underscores the urgent need for effective interventions. Probiotics have gained attention as a promising strategy to combat these viral infections due to their potential in...

title: Vitamin D Supplementation in Community-Dwelling Adults.
abstract: Vitamin D testing is commonly performed in adults. Evidence is lacking to support vitamin D screening or supplementation in the general population, regardless of baseline serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels. The National Academy of Medicine recommends that individuals 70 years and younger consume 600 IU of vitamin D daily and that individuals older than 70 years consume 800 IU daily. This can be achieved through dietary sources, supplements, or both. Achieving the recommended intake prevents serum ...

title: The Effects of Multi-Strain Probiotic SLAB51 Intake on Aerobic Performance and Oxidative Stress Responses in Elite Athletes: A Randomized Crossover Trial.
abstract: Exercise performance and recovery depend on interactions between energy metabolism and redox regulation. SLAB51, a multi-strain probiotic, may influence oxygen-related metabolism and antioxidant responses, but evidence in elite athletes remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of SLAB51 supplementation on aerobic exercise capacity and oxidative stress responses in elite athletes.

title: Daily Patterns in the Timing of Medication and Supplement Intake.
abstract: Background/Objectives: The timing of medication intake can influence therapeutic efficacy and adverse effects, yet little is known about when medications are actually taken in daily life. We aimed to characterize real-world temporal patterns of medication and dietary supplement use at the population level. Methods: We analyzed time-stamped medication and dietary supplement records from 26,069 adults enrolled in the myCircadianClock smartphone application, generating a population-scale atlas of r...

title: The Gut Microbiota as a Mediator of the Metabolic Benefits of Fungi and Their Polysaccharides: A Review of Evidence Addressing Causality.
abstract: Prebiotic supplementation has emerged as a promising strategy to ameliorate metabolic disorders through beneficial reshaping of the gut microbiota. Accumulating evidence suggests that fungi and their polysaccharides (e.g., those from Auricularia auricula-judae, Boletus edulis, Hirsutella sinensis, Isaria cicadae, Ramaria botrytoides, and Wolfiporia cocos) possess considerable potential in this context. The present review summarizes studies providing data relevant to the potential involvement of ...

title: Exercise-Induced Dehydration Limits the Effectiveness of Post-Exercise Whey Protein Supplementation in Healthy Young Men.
abstract: Post-exercise protein ingestion is widely used to promote recovery from exercise, but whether exercise-induced dehydration limits the subsequent protein supplementation response remains unclear. This study examined the effects of different hydration strategies during exercise on post-exercise whey protein supplementation.

title: Dietary Omega-3 Intake, Supplement Use and Omega-3 Status in Elite (Tier 3) Male Gaelic Football Players: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-3PUFA) are recognised for their roles in cardiovascular and brain health, with emerging evidence suggesting potential benefits for athletic performance and recovery. However, dietary intake and biological status of n-3PUFA remain poorly understood in athletes from intermittent team sports in Ireland, such as Gaelic football players. Through combining self-reported intake and biological assessment, this study provides, to our knowledge...

title: Effects of Body-Mass-Scaled Protein and Leucine Supplementation on Body Composition and Cardiometabolic Blood Markers During Weight Loss in Older Men-A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Background: Overweight and obesity are burgeoning health epidemics. Diets including alternate-day fasting (ADF) promote weight loss but risk significant muscle loss, posing health implications to seniors at risk of sarcopenia. Leucine, the key muscle protein synthesis (MPS) driver, effectively stimulates MPS with lower calorie intake than protein. However, the effects of body-mass-scaled protein and leucine intakes are unclear. Objectives: To evaluate body-mass-scaled leucine or protein suppleme...

title: Longitudinal Trajectories of Physical and Mental Health-Related Quality of Life Following Psychobiotic Supplementation in Gastrointestinal Oncology Patients: A Post Hoc Analysis of the ProDeCa Study.
abstract: Patients undergoing surgery followed by adjuvant chemotherapy for gastrointestinal cancer frequently experience impaired health-related quality of life (HR-QoL). This post hoc analysis of the ProDeCa randomized trial investigated whether psychobiotic treatment was associated with longitudinal changes in HR-QoL.

title: Nutritional Management of Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome: Current Evidence on Dietary Strategies, Supplementation, and Lifestyle Support.
abstract: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), formerly known as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is a heterogeneous endocrine and metabolic disorder associated with reproductive dysfunction, hyperandrogenism, insulin resistance, chronic low-grade inflammation and an increased risk of long-term cardiometabolic disease. Lifestyle intervention remains the cornerstone of management; however, the optimal nutritional strategy continues to be debated. This narrative review summarizes current eviden...

title: Effects of Probiotic Supplementation on Performance Retention During Detraining and Recovery After Simulated Return-to-Training Stress in College Volleyball Players: An Exploratory Randomized, Single-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
abstract: Background: The effects of probiotic supplementation on performance and recovery during training transitions remain uncertain. This exploratory trial examined the effects of probiotic supplementation on performance, recovery, and gut microbiota in national-level university volleyball players. Methods: Twenty-eight players were randomized to receive a multi-strain probiotic or placebo (n = 14 per group) for 8 weeks, comprising regular training, tapering and competition, and reduced training. Perf...

title: Effects of Acute Carbohydrate-Electrolyte Supplementation on Exercise Performance in Moderate-to-Hot Ambient Conditions: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: An ambient-temperature eligibility criterion of ≥22 °C was treated as an operational lower boundary spanning moderate or mildly warm to hot conditions, not as a universal physiological threshold for heat stress. This systematic review and three-level meta-analysis evaluated acute carbohydrate-electrolyte (CHO-E) supplementation versus a water or non-caloric placebo during exercise at these temperatures.

title: Heat-Inactivated Lacticaseibacillus paracasei PC-01 Alleviates DSS-Induced Colitis in Mice by Modulating Gut Microbiota and Intestinal Barrier Function.
abstract: Background: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic, progressive, immune-mediated inflammatory disorder of the gastrointestinal tract. Methods: This study used C57BL/6J mice induced by DSS to construct an intestinal inflammation model, and explored the alleviating effect and potential mechanism of heat inactivated Lactobacillus paracasei PC-01 (PC-01) on intestinal inflammation. Results: The results showed that heat-inactivated PC-01 significantly decreased the Disease Activity Index and H...

title: A Pilot Proof-of-Concept Study to Evaluate the Physiological and Cognitive Impacts of Hericium erinaceus on Healthy Adults.
abstract: Background: Executive function is a critical component of cognitive health that supports goal-directed behavior, attentional control, and cognitive flexibility. These processes are sensitive to aging and lifestyle factors and may be modifiable through nutritional strategies. Hericium Erinaceus (lion's mane; LM) is an edible mushroom containing bioactive compounds shown to stimulate neurotrophins such as brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), suggesting potential cognitive benefits. Methods: T...

title: The Effects of Combined Caffeine and Sodium Bicarbonate Supplementation on Exercise Performance, Physiological Responses, and Gastrointestinal Tolerability: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Background: Caffeine and sodium bicarbonate can individually enhance exercise performance, but whether their combined use provides additional benefits and how it affects physiological responses and gastrointestinal (GI) tolerability remain unclear. Objective: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of combined caffeine and sodium bicarbonate (CAF + SB) supplementation on exercise performance, physiological responses, and GI tolerability, and to determine whether it...

title: Supplementation of Bacillus cereus Enhances Anti-Colitis Effects of Triple Probiotics in Mice: Correlative Evidence for a Gut Microbiota-Spermidine-Related Axis in Quadruple-Probiotic Protection.
abstract: Background: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic relapsing inflammatory bowel disease associated with gut microbiota dysbiosis. The triple-probiotic mixture BLE (Bifidobacterium infantis, Lactobacillus acidophilus, Enterococcus faecalis) contains highly oxygen-sensitive strains prone to viability loss during gastrointestinal transit. Adding facultative-aerobic Bacillus cereus generates a four-strain probiotic formulation BLEB. This study aimed to determine whether adding B. cereus improves the a...

title: Ketoanalogues of Essential Amino Acids in Chronic Kidney Disease: From Biochemical Rationale to Conditions for Clinical Effectiveness.
abstract: Protein restriction is an established nutritional intervention for selected adults with non-dialysis chronic kidney disease (CKD); a supplemented very-low-protein diet (sVLPD) combines marked protein restriction with essential amino acids and their nitrogen-free keto- and hydroxyanalogues (KAs). KAs may accept amino groups and regenerate essential amino acids while limiting exogenous nitrogen, but reversible transamination competes with irreversible oxidative decarboxylation. This narrative revi...

title: Dietary Zinc Glycine Supplementation Attenuates Aging-Driven Cochlear Hair Cell Oxidative Injury and Hearing Loss.
abstract: Background: Micronutrient imbalance is now recognized as a modifiable risk factor driving the progression of age-related hearing loss (ARHL). Zinc, an indispensable dietary trace nutrient, acts as a structural cofactor and transcriptional regulator of a broad panel of antioxidant enzymes to sustain systemic and cellular antioxidant defense capacity. Nevertheless, the therapeutic value of zinc nutritional supplementation and its precise molecular mechanisms against age-dependent cochlear degenera...

title: Iron Supplementation and Copper Homeostasis: Evidence for Potential Copper Depletion, Biomarker Challenges, and Clinical Implications.
abstract: Iron deficiency remains a major nutritional problem, particularly among women of reproductive age, pregnant women, infants, and children. Oral iron supplementation is the principal strategy for prevention and treatment, but the biological interdependence of iron and copper metabolism raises concern that prolonged or excessive iron exposure may impair copper availability in susceptible individuals. This review summarizes human and animal evidence linking iron supplementation or high dietary iron ...

title: Synbiotic HQP08 Supplementation for Hair Loss and Depressive Symptoms: An Open-Label Pilot Study of Clinical Outcomes and Gut Microbiome Changes.
abstract: Background: Gut microbiota dysregulation has been implicated in hair loss via the gut-skin axis, but human interventional data are limited. We previously showed that Bifidobacterium longum HK003 reverses alopecia-like phenotypes in mice. Methods: We conducted an open-label, single-arm pilot study to evaluate an HK003-containing synbiotic (HQP08) in 32 adults with self-reported hair loss over 8 weeks. The primary endpoint was the proportion of participants reporting improvement on the Patient Glo...

title: Probiotics in Celiac Disease: Current Evidence and Future Directions.
abstract: Celiac disease is often associated with gut microbiome alterations, which may play a role in autoimmunity to gluten peptides and upregulation of other autoinflammatory pathways. Probiotics of various formulations have been evaluated in attempts to normalize the gut microbiome and/or improve symptoms in Celiac disease, and even to potentially prevent Celiac disease in at-risk individuals. These studies have shown mixed results at best, and conclusions about the effectiveness of probiotics to thes...

title: Beyond Taxonomy: Fungal Nutraceutical Supplementation Modifies the Functional Potential of the Gut Microbiome in Colorectal Cancer.
abstract: The gut microbiome is increasingly recognized as an important determinant of host immune regulation, intestinal homeostasis, and recovery after colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery. Although our previous randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial demonstrated that fungal nutraceutical supplementation with Micodigest® was associated with favorable taxonomic and systemic inflammatory changes in patients undergoing CRC surgery with curative intent, the functional consequences of this in...

title: Bioprospecting of Cheese Whey: Isolation, Safety and Cytoprotective Effects of Limosilactobacillus fermentum Strains on Intestinal Cells.
abstract: Bioprospecting is the identification and exploitation of natural resources for commercial purposes. Cheese whey is a major dairy by-product rich in nutrients and a possible source of bioactive compounds. The aim of this study was to isolate and identify lactic acid bacteria from cheese whey and characterize them based on their probiotic and technological properties, together with their cytotoxicity and cytoprotective effect on intestinal epithelial cells. From 142 isolates, three were selected a...

title: Dietary Selenium-Enriched Bacillus subtilis Improves Feed Utilization and Modulates Selected Responses to LPS Challenge in Laying Hens.
abstract: This study evaluated the effects of dietary selenium-enriched Bacillus subtilis (HBS) supplementation on laying performance, egg quality, and responses to lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge. A total of 120 Jinghong-1 laying hens received a basal or HBS-supplemented diet for 12 weeks. Subsequently, hens within each dietary replicate were allocated to phosphate-buffered saline (PBS)- or LPS-injected subgroups, and one hen per subgroup was sampled 12 h after injection, yielding six sampled hens per...

title: Early-Life Oat Supplementation Is Associated with Altered Cecal Microbiota and Microbial Metabolic Profiles and Reduced Campylobacter jejuni Colonization in Broiler Chickens.
abstract: Campylobacter jejuni is a leading foodborne pathogen that commonly colonizes the intestinal tract of broiler chickens and represents a significant food safety concern. Dietary intervention may provide a practical approach to modulate the gut microbiota and reduce pathogen colonization. This study investigated the effects of oat supplementation on C. jejuni colonization and dissemination, cecal microbiota and predicted functions, and cecal short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) and ileal amino acid prof...

title: Targeting the Gut Vascular Axis in Atherosclerosis: Probiotic and Phytoantioxidant Crosstalk as a Hypothesis-Generating Framework for Residual Cardiovascular Risk.
abstract: Despite decades of effective statin therapy, a clinically important proportion of patients with atherosclerosis continue to experience ischemic events, even when low-density-lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is at guideline-recommended levels. This shortfall is increasingly attributed to residual inflammatory, oxidative, and gut microbial pathways that lipid lowering therapy was never designed to address. This review establishes the mechanistic rationale for combining two emerging dietary interven...

title: Insights into the Health-Promoting Properties and Nutraceutical and Food Applications of Lonicera japonica Thunb.
abstract: Lonicera japonica Thunb. (L. japonica), an edible medicinal plant that has been widely consumed in East Asian countries, including China, Japan, and Korea, for centuries, has long been regarded as a superior herb in traditional Chinese medicine and is an economically important crop commonly used in beverages, foods, and herbal medicines. Extensive studies have demonstrated that L. japonica possesses a broad spectrum of health-promoting properties, including antioxidant, antibacterial, antiviral,...

title: Heat-Inactivated Lactiplantibacillus plantarum (RSB11) as a Multifunctional Postbiotic: Anti-Inflammatory Effects Compared with Live RSB11 Across Multiple Human Cell Models.
abstract: The clinical potential of probiotics is increasingly recognized; however, dependence on microbial viability, formulation and storage constraints, and safety considerations in vulnerable populations can limit their broader application. Postbiotics offer an alternative by providing inanimate microbial preparations with retained biological activity, yet whether heat inactivation preserves the functional effects of probiotic-derived candidates remains an important question. Here, we compare Lactipla...

title: Short-term Rhodiola rosea supplementation improves premenstrual symptoms, reaction time, and perceived exertion in female taekwondo athletes: a randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial.
abstract: Premenstrual symptoms may negatively influence psychological readiness, cognitive-motor performance, and perceived exertion in female athletes. Rhodiola rosea (RR) is an adaptogenic herb that has been investigated for its potential effects on fatigue, stress tolerance, mood, and exercise-related outcomes. However, its effects on premenstrual symptoms and performance-related responses in female athletes remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the effects of short-term RR supplementation d...
journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

title: Probiotic microcapsule polysaccharide-protein composite system: construction, mechanism and application.
abstract: Microencapsulation technology can effectively protect the activity of endogenous probiotics, extend the shelf life of probiotics, and achieve their targeted release in vitro. Therefore, it has been widely used in the field of food processing. However, the complex food environment requires careful selection of microcapsule synthesis methods and materials. Polysaccharide-protein composite microcapsules represent a popular strategy for probiotic protection. However, most existing studies evaluate t...

title: Alternative splicing dynamics in pig tissues under soybean oil supplementation.
abstract: Lipid metabolism in pigs is a relevant model for understanding human metabolic regulation due to physiological similarities between the species. Alternative splicing (AS) generates transcript variants that can modulate metabolic pathways in the brain, liver, and skeletal muscle. This study aimed to identify and characterize AS events to explore the dynamics of AS under supplementation of soybean oil in these three tissues. We performed RNA sequencing in 36 pigs fed a soybean-corn diet supplement...
journal: Mammalian genome : official journal of the International Mammalian Genome Society

title: Cross-Cultural Adaptation and Psychometric Evaluation of the Turkish DESTEK (D-SCOPE) Questionnaire: A Multidimensional Assessment of Dietitians' Knowledge, Attitudes and Preparedness Regarding Dietary Supplements in Türkiye.
abstract: The increasing use of dietary supplements in Türkiye underscores the need for validated instruments to assess dietitians' knowledge, attitudes and self-efficacy regarding supplements. However, no validated Turkish tool is currently available. This study aimed to culturally adapt the Dietitians' Survey of Comfort, Opinions and Preparedness in Education in Supplements (-SCOPE) Questionnaire into Turkish (Diyetisyenlerin Eğitim, Supleman Tercihleri ve Konforu Anketi; DESTEK) and evaluate its psycho...
journal: Journal of human nutrition and dietetics : the official journal of the British Dietetic Association

title: Integrating probiotics into a one-day diabetes clinic: outcomes in gestational diabetes.
abstract: To investigate the effects of a one-day diabetes clinic management model combined with probiotic supplementation in patients with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM).

title: In vitro assessment of the probiotic potential and safety of lactic acid bacteria for aquatic animal health.
abstract: This study evaluated the in vitro probiotic-related properties and preliminary safety profiles of five lactic acid bacteria (LAB) strains for potential use in aquaculture: Limosilactobacillus reuteri ATCC 55730, Lentilactobacillus kefiri K107, Latilactobacillus sakei SN34, Lactiplantibacillus plantarum FI8595, and Streptococcus thermophilus BioSt64. Probiotic-related traits included antimicrobial activity against Lactococcus garvieae and Yersinia ruckeri, aggregation-related properties, and tole...

title: Enriching Activated Charcoal With Aged Palm Sap Improves Laying Hen Performance, Egg Quality, and Reproductive Function.
abstract: This study evaluated the effects of activated charcoal (AC) and aged palm sap-enriched AC (AC + APS) on laying performance, egg quality, reproductive physiology, hematology, and serum biochemistry of laying hens alongside physicochemical characterization of the additives. Two hundred and forty Isa Brown hens were assigned to five dietary treatments: control, 0.5% AC, 1.0% AC, 0.5% AC + APS, and 1.0% AC + APS during a 12-week feeding trial. High-performance liquid chromatography identified glucos...
journal: Animal science journal = Nihon chikusan Gakkaiho

title: Knowledge and attitudes as correlates of dietary supplement use among adults in Saudi Arabia: a cross-sectional online survey of a predominantly Riyadh-based convenience sample.
abstract: Dietary supplement (DS) use is widespread in Saudi Arabia, but high prevalence does not by itself indicate informed use.

title: Microbiome-based probiotic intervention to reduce chemotherapy-induced gastrointestinal toxicity.
abstract: Chemotherapy is one of the primary treatment options for cancer; however, its gastrointestinal toxicity and disruption of gut microbial homeostasis can adversely affect patient health and treatment outcomes. This study investigated chemotherapy-induced alterations in the gut microbiome and evaluated the effects of probiotic supplementation on microbial diversity, gastrointestinal toxicity, and treatment response in cancer patients.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

title: Saccharomyces boulardii reduces food intake and attenuates weight gain in diet-induced obese mice: links to gut microbial, metabolic, and immune remodeling.
abstract: The gut microbiome is a key regulator of metabolic homeostasis and contributes to obesity progression through effects on immune signaling, gut barrier integrity, and systemic inflammation. Microbiome-targeted strategies are therefore being explored as complementary approaches to conventional weight-loss therapies. Here, we investigated whether the probiotic yeast Saccharomyces boulardii modulates the gut-immune-metabolic axis in diet-induced obesity (DIO).

title: Modulation of Early-Life Calf Gut Microbiota by Bacteriocin-Producing Lactiplantibacillus pentosus AA86 and Pediococcus pentosaceus AA94.
abstract: Early-life gut microbiota plays a critical role in livestock health and productivity. Probiotic interventions, particularly those employing bacteriocin-producing lactic acid bacteria (LAB), may contribute to modulation of microbial development during this critical period. This study evaluated Lactiplantibacillus pentosus AA86 (formerly Lactobacillus pentosus) and Pediococcus pentosaceus AA94 for genomic safety, bacteriocin potential, and their effects on calf gut microbiota. Whole-genome sequenc...

title: Impact of probiotic supplementation on serum klotho levels and inflammatory status in patients with diabetic kidney disease.
abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) involves complex metabolic and inflammatory pathways, where gut dysbiosis via the gut-kidney axis plays a critical pathophysiological role. Probiotics may resolve renal decline and modulate aging biomarkers, but clinical evidence in DKD remains limited. This study evaluated the effects of Lactobacillus supplementation on serum alpha-Klotho levels, systemic inflammation, and renal biomarkers DKD patients. In an open-label, parallel-group controlled clinical trial, co...

title: Load and breath-hold: impact of 7-day creatine monohydrate loading on breath-hold exercise performance - a double-blind randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Creatine supplementation enhances anaerobic energy availability and buffering capacity; however, its impact on muscle work under voluntary breath-hold (BH) remains unexplored. BH exercise increases reliance on anaerobic ATP production and creates a metabolic environment in which phosphocreatine-derived ATP may be particularly valuable. The aim of this study was to determine whether creatine monohydrate loading improves BH exercise performance in trained BH divers.
journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

title: Remodeling the gut microbiota: mechanistic insights into probiotic-mediated alleviation of weaning stress in piglets.
abstract: Early weaning, characterized by the replacement of maternal milk with solid diets, is widely recognized as one of the most stressful developmental events affecting piglets in intensive production systems. During this stage, the digestive, immune, and metabolic systems remain immature, rendering piglets highly susceptible to environmental and nutritional stressors as well as opportunistic pathogens. These challenges frequently disrupt intestinal microbial homeostasis, impair gut barrier integrity...

title: Research progress on intestinal probiotics-mediated protection of the intestinal mucosal barrier in ulcerative colitis.
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a major subtype of inflammatory bowel disease characterized by a chronic, relapsing course. Its pathogenesis involves complex interactions among gut microbial dysbiosis, epithelial barrier disruption, dysregulated immune responses, and oxidative stress. Impairment of the intestinal mucosal barrier facilitates the translocation of luminal antigens, bacteria, and microbial metabolites into the mucosa, thereby aggravating local inflammation. Probiotics may help maintain b...

title: Omega-3 supplementation during pregnancy in relation to reported information sources: an exploratory cross-sectional study.
abstract: Omega-3 fatty acid supplementation during pregnancy is recommended in certain settings and may be relevant for maternal and fetal health, yet uptake varies widely. While educational attainment is commonly considered a determinant of health behavior, the relationship between reported information sources and supplementation practices during pregnancy remains insufficiently understood.

title: Comparative effectiveness of dietary supplements in dilated cardiomyopathy: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
abstract: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a major cause of heart failure and cardiovascular mortality, partly due to impaired myocardial energy metabolism. Dietary supplements may offer benefits through improved mitochondrial function and antioxidant effects, and randomized controlled trials (RCTs) suggest they can enhance cardiac function in DCM. However, direct comparisons among supplements are lacking, and the optimal strategy and dose-response relationship remain undetermined.

title: Relationship between neonatal glutamine supplementation and amino acid profiles, protein synthesis in splanchnic tissues and the plasma metabolome in 5-day-old piglets with low birth weight.
abstract: The incidence of low birthweight (LBiW) piglets, which show impaired growth compared to normal birthweight (NBiW) littermates, has increased with litter size. We previously reported that glutamine increased the bodyweight and plasma glutamine concentrations in LBiW piglets, with no effect on jejunal glutamine concentrations or glutamine transport and metabolism mRNA abundance. In this study, we investigated the effect of glutamine supplementation on proteinogenic free amino acid (FAA), protein-b...

title: Patient satisfaction and adherence to vitamin D supplementation: results from a nationwide survey in Italy.
abstract: The objective of the present study was to evaluate patient satisfaction and adherence to different vitamin D formulations and dosing regimens in a large Italian cohort of patients treated for osteoporosis or vitamin D deficiency.
